en: The Jātaka:
The Twelfth Chapter,
The Minor Section on Kuṇāla.
4. The Kāma Jātaka:
“If one who desires sensual pleasure succeeds in obtaining that which they desire;”
Truly, a mortal becomes joyful in mind when he obtains what he desires;
yet for one who longs for sensual pleasures—
If that succeeds for him,
he thereafter finds no further sensual pleasures,
just as one finds no thirst in the heat.
Just as the horn of a horned bull grows as it grows,
so too does the ignorance of a foolish person increase.
For the fool who lacks understanding,
craving and thirst increase even further as he grows in age.
Even by giving the entire earth with its rice and barley,
its cattle, horses, slaves, and servants,
it would not be enough for even one person.
Knowing this, one should live equanimously.
A king, having conquered the earth by force and dwelling upon the great earth bounded by the ocean;
One who is not yet satiated with this ocean would long even for the further shore;
so it is with one who keeps recollecting sensual pleasures.
One does not find satisfaction by means of the mind alone;
having turned back and desisted from that,
one sees that those who are satisfied by wisdom are truly satisfied.
One satisfied with wisdom is the best;
such a person is not satiated by sensual pleasures.
A person satisfied with wisdom—
Craving does not gain mastery over one who diminishes sensual desires,
who has few wishes, and is free from greed.
A man who is as vast as the ocean is not satiated by sensual pleasures,
just as a leather-worker is never sated with hides.
A sandal worn out by constant use;
whatever one relinquishes among sensual pleasures,
that very thing results in happiness.
“If one should desire all happiness,
one should renounce all sensual pleasures.
“Eight verses were spoken by you;”
All are thousands strong;
accept them, Great Brahmā,
let this word of yours be fulfilled.”
“I have no need for thousands,
nor for hundreds or tens of thousands;
having spoken this final verse, [I shall depart].”
“My mind finds no delight in sensual pleasures.
“Truly auspicious is this young man,
the Sage who knows all the world!”
“The wise person who fully understands this craving, the mother of suffering.
The Fourth Kāma Jātaka.
